data_requests.item: Existing named-valve and bypass function, characteristic and operating basis
where: site records: Existing named-valve sizing/Cv and characteristic, process/system/pump duty and pressure/flow range, control-performance and bypass function/normal-position records. Retain exact asset/source/revision, availability and operating/sample coverage; do not substitute another site or valve.
historian or DCS trend for FV-A (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)

a walkdown: Only if existing records cannot settle an applicable question: agree safe observations with the responsible engineer, including actual bypass function/position or measured travel association. No automatic field test, bypass closure or equipment change.
data_requests.how: First establish the actual valve/bypass service and association: same-stream presence does not prove a physical bypass around this valve. Distinguish command/indication from measured valve travel, and review the valve characteristic and matched operating/control-performance basis. Low opening, an open/cracked bypass or a source example alone does not prove oversizing or justify resize/trim; bypasses can perform legitimate differential-pressure protection or temperature control. Acknowledge suitable existing records without compulsory new measurement; retain unknown or foreign/unavailable evidence as qualified context.

questions.decision_rule: Review whether existing service, valve characteristic, system/pump operating range, control performance and actual bypass purpose establish a remaining investigation. No universal 50%-open criterion, commanded position, cracked bypass or absent record authorizes resize/trim, bypass closure or other hardware/operating change. Suitable existing records may be acknowledged; unresolved applicability or association remains a records question for the responsible engineer.

typical_benefit.wording: S13, printed pp. 25–26: highly throttled operation is a clue to review pump/system duty, valve sizing, characterization and control performance. Bypasses can have protective or temperature-control functions. This source supports investigation, not a universal opening threshold or a quantified site benefit.
source_titles: S13: Improving Pumping System Performance: A Sourcebook for Industry, 2nd ed. (DOE + Hydraulic Institute; DOE/GO-102006-2079)

questions.limits: Source-informed records review: S13 printed pp. 25–26 / PDF pp. 29–30, including valve-characterization qualifications and protective/temperature bypass functions. The earlier ellipsis omitted intervening characterization context; its exact old wording remains in history. Opening or a bypass label alone does not establish suitability, source authority or permission to modify equipment. Supplied fields remain candidates.
